headline: Europe considers keeping young children off social media

sources.title: EU to limit children's access to social media
EU plans to ban under-13s from social media, with 'phased access' afterwards
EU chief weighs age restrictions for children using social media

chunks.text: A [[growing number of]] governments are trying to {{clamp down}} on children's use of social media. The trend {{kicked off}} in Australia, which {{rolled out}} a [[ban]] on the apps for anyone under 16. Now the European Union is thinking about a similar [[policy]] for the young people in its member countries. Leaders say the plan is [[meant to]] protect [[minors]] from [[harm]].

verbs.correct: To take strong action to stop or control something
verbs.wrong: To punish people who have already broken an existing rule

verbs.correct: To start or begin an event or activity
To officially start or introduce something new
verbs.wrong: To slowly cancel a rule that is no longer needed

chunks.text: Under the new idea, children under 13 would not be able to {{sign up}} for social media at all. After that age, teenagers would [[gradually]] be allowed to join, but only once the [[platforms]] {{carry out}} stronger safety checks. Ursula von der Leyen, who {{heads up}} the European Commission, said the plan is not about stopping children from using the apps. She said it is really about deciding when the apps can reach into children's lives.

verbs.correct: To join or register for a service or activity
verbs.wrong: To formally agree to follow a set of rules

verbs.correct: To do or perform a task, often one that was planned

verbs.correct: To be the leader of a group or organization

chunks.text: People who support the rules point to studies that connect [[heavy]] app use with worse [[mental health]] among teenagers. They [[argue]] that the apps are built to {{draw in}} young users and keep them scrolling for hours. To deal with this, the EU may make companies {{turn off}} features like [[autoplay]] and endless scrolling. Many parents also worry about the anxiety and lost sleep that come with [[constant]] use.

verbs.correct: To attract someone and get their interest
verbs.wrong: To trap someone so that they cannot escape

verbs.correct: To stop a machine or feature from working
verbs.wrong: To remove something completely and permanently

chunks.text: Not everyone {{goes along with}} the plans. Some experts warn that [[strict]] [[age checks]] could put everyone's [[privacy]] [[at risk]], since websites would need to gather more personal information. Others say a ban might {{shut out}} young people from useful advice, support groups, and online friends. The EU is expected to {{put forward}} a formal [[proposal]] after the summer break, and countries around the world are watching to see [[what happens next]].

tf.s: Australia brought in a ban on social media for children under 16.
tf.why: The story says the trend kicked off in Australia, which brought in a ban for anyone under 16.

tf.s: The EU wants to shut out all teenagers over 13 from social media forever.
tf.why: The ban would be for children under 13. After that age, teenagers would gradually be allowed to join once platforms are safer.

tf.s: Under the plan, children under 13 could still freely sign up for any social media app.
tf.why: False. Under the new idea, children under 13 would not be able to sign up for social media at all.

tf.s: Everyone goes along with the EU's plan without any worries.
tf.why: Not everyone goes along with the plans, and some experts warn that age checks could put people's privacy at risk.
